title: Load balancers
hook: One public door, many identical servers behind it — the balancer picks who answers.

steps.caption: Your request hits the load balancer, not a single app server.

nodeCaptions.lb: Health checks and algorithms (round-robin, least connections…) choose a backend.

steps.caption: It forwards to one healthy server — today, Server 2.

nodeCaptions.s2: You didn’t pick Server 2 — the balancer did.
nodeCaptions.s1: Idle this request; ready for the next.

takeaways: Load balancers spread traffic so no single server is the only path.
Clients usually talk to a virtual address in front of many backends.
Health checks keep broken servers out of rotation.

quiz.question: What problem does a load balancer mainly solve?
choices: Assigning IP addresses on your LAN
quiz.explanation: Distribution and failover — not application business logic.
